authorship: AI-authored synthetic; no telecom expert review

customer_checks: Ask which light on the fibre box is red: LOS, PON or Power. Record whether the power light stays on.
Ask whether nearby customers also lost service; do not disconnect, bend or look into the fibre cable.
BB01.title: Red LOS light or optical signal loss
BB01.diagnostic_gate: an optical test finds no received signal, the account is active, and a technician confirms an external-line fault
BB01.agent_checks: Ask provider support to check account and area-outage status, test the optical signal, and identify whether the external line or fibre box needs repair.
BB01.action: request an authorised technician to inspect and repair the confirmed external-line fault
BB01.completion: the fibre box shows the normal connection indicators for its model and a connected device can browse again

customer_checks: Record when the account or plan migration completed and whether service ever worked afterwards.
Record the fibre-box light labels and whether both wired and wireless devices lack internet.
Record the affected street or building and when customers first lost service.
Collect reports from other affected locations; do not ask each customer to reset equipment.
BB03.title: Shared broadband outage across a street or building
BB03.agent_checks: Ask network support to match the affected locations to an active provider incident and record the confirmed update reference.
BB03.completion: the provider records incident recovery and affected customers confirm browsing works again

customer_checks: Record the move date and whether internet has worked at the new address.
Ask support to match the installed fibre box to the new-address order using its secure account workflow.
Record the invoice, payment dates and approximate amounts; do not collect card numbers or banking passwords.
Ask whether both payments are settled or one is still pending; a pending hold is not a confirmed duplicate payment.
BD01.title: Two settled payments for one invoice
BD01.agent_checks: Ask billing support to match both settled payment entries to the same invoice and rule out a pending bank hold or a different invoice.
BD01.diagnostic_gate: the ledger confirms two settled payments against the same invoice
BD01.action: ask authorised billing staff to reconcile the duplicate and initiate the approved adjustment
BD01.completion: one valid invoice payment remains and billing records the duplicate adjustment with a reference

customer_checks: Record the add-on name, charge period and when the customer first noticed it.
Ask whether the customer recalls accepting the add-on and through which channel; do not treat recollection as proof of consent.
Record the old plan, new plan and effective change date shown on the bill.
Compare the start and end dates of each billed period before treating two line items as duplicate charges.
Record the cancellation confirmation date and the effective end date shown in the notice.
Identify the billed period after cancellation; keep any genuinely used service period separate.
Ask whether the router power light is off, intermittent or steady, and whether the socket powers another safe appliance.
Record the power-adapter label without opening it or substituting an unapproved supply.
Record the router model, update time and light pattern after the failed update.
Keep the device powered as directed by its approved support guide; do not install an image downloaded from an unverified site.
Ask whether the router is in an enclosed space or has blocked ventilation, and whether it feels unusually hot.
Keep it in a safe ventilated position; stop using it if there is smoke, a burning smell or visible damage.
Record which Ethernet port and device are affected and whether Wi-Fi or another port still works.
If safe and not already tried, compare using a known-good Ethernet cable and another available port.
Record the start and end of each interruption and whether it coincides with wet weather.
Ask whether a wired device also loses internet during the same interruption; record the fibre-box light labels.
ID01.title: Intermittent line loss after wet weather
ID01.agent_checks: Ask line support to compare optical-loss logs with the reported interruption times. If line loss is present, request a technician to inspect external joints for moisture.
ID01.diagnostic_gate: optical loss events align with rain and a technician finds moisture at an external joint
ID01.action: have an authorised technician repair and seal the confirmed damaged joint
ID01.completion: line monitoring shows no optical-loss events during a later wet-weather check and the customer reports no repeat drop

customer_checks: Record when the evening drops start, how long they last, and whether the connection drops or only slows.
Ask whether a wired device also loses internet during the evening problem; do not repeat a completed wired test.
ID02.title: Evening connection drops: check access-network congestion
ID02.agent_checks: Ask network support whether the line stays connected during the evening problem and whether monitoring shows congestion on the local access segment.
ID02.diagnostic_gate: the line stays synchronized and provider monitoring shows peak-hour congestion on the access segment
ID02.action: ask network operations to rebalance the affected capacity and monitor the next busy period
ID02.completion: the next evening wired check shows no repeat packet loss or dropped calls

customer_checks: Record the interval between interruptions and whether the router stays powered.
Ask whether wired and wireless devices stop at the same time; record any session error shown by the router.
Ask whether the fibre box loses power or restarts during the interruption; a green router light does not prove the fibre box is healthy.
Record the adapter label and any power-light changes without opening the adapter or trying a different voltage supply.
ID04.title: Fibre-box power interruptions: check the approved adapter
ID04.agent_checks: Ask an authorised technician to test the fibre-box power adapter under load; the customer should not open the adapter or measure live electrical connections.
ID04.diagnostic_gate: an authorised technician reproduces voltage drops with the ONT power adapter
ID04.action: have the technician replace it with the provider-approved matching adapter
ID04.completion: the fibre box stays powered and the internet session remains stable during observation

customer_checks: Record whether calls or data fail indoors, outdoors or in both locations.
If possible, compare another compatible device at the same location; do not interpret one weak-signal report as a network outage.
Record the affected location, start time and whether other nearby subscribers are affected.
Ask whether calls, SMS and data are all affected; retain any working services in the report.
Record the operator name shown in network-selection settings and the location of the failure.
Ask whether the customer recently selected an operator manually; do not change settings without consent.
Record the handset model, location and whether the problem follows the phone to other locations.
If the customer can safely do so, record a compatible known-good SIM cross-test; do not request SIM security codes in chat.
Record the device model, data error and whether calls or SMS still work.
Ask support to compare the APN with the provider's current authenticated device guide; do not invent APN values.
Record the plan and the usage shown in the provider app for the current billing period.
Check whether the slowdown began after the displayed allowance was used; retain the customer's observed speeds.
Ask whether the phone uses one SIM or two and which subscription is selected for mobile data.
Confirm which subscription has active data service before changing its preference with consent.
Record the purchased plan, change date and when data stopped working.
Ask support to check the purchased data entitlement and verify that the device APN is correct.
Record the rejected transfer status and the reason given by the provider.
Use a secure support channel to verify the donor account details; do not ask for identity documents in this chat.
Record the accepted transfer status and scheduled date shown by the provider.
Confirm whether the old service still works and whether the recorded transfer window has elapsed.
Record which originating networks can and cannot reach the transferred number.
Collect approximate failed-call times for a routing trace; do not claim a particular operator is at fault without a trace.
Record the transfer order status and authorization-expiry message.
Guide the customer to the provider's authenticated authorization workflow; never collect the authorization code in this chat.
Record the bill payment date and the current service restriction shown by the provider.
Ask whether the payment is settled; a receipt alone does not establish that restoration reached the network.
Record the payment status shown by the bank and provider without collecting account or card credentials.
Separate a pending authorization from a settled payment before advising another payment.
Record which customer-owned account should have received the payment.
Ask billing support to trace the payment through its secure ownership-verification workflow.
Record the restriction message and whether the provider confirms the invoice is paid.
Ask which review team owns the restriction; do not assume another payment will clear a non-billing hold.
Record the visited country, purchased roaming pack and whether calls or SMS work.
Ask support to verify that roaming data is enabled on the account; device roaming alone does not establish account eligibility.
Record the visited country and selected local operator.
Ask support to check the current partner list for the customer's plan; do not invent a supported operator name.
Record the purchased pack's start date, end date and the customer's travel dates.
Check whether the current date is within the displayed validity period before changing or buying a pack.
Record the pack's displayed remaining data and validity period.
Check whether an additional entitlement is already active before suggesting a paid top-up.
Record the activation order status and whether the physical SIM has ever worked.
Ask activation support to compare the order and SIM identifier through its authenticated workflow.
Record the eSIM activation error and whether the profile was already downloaded to another device.
Use the authenticated transfer workflow; do not share or repeatedly scan a private activation QR code in this chat.
Record the activation status and the outstanding verification task shown by the provider.
Direct the customer to the secure verification workflow; do not collect identity documents here.
Record the exact device variant and the eSIM error.
Check the provider's current supported-device list before recommending another profile download.
Record which sender's messages are missing, approximate request times and whether ordinary SMS arrives.
Ask the customer to check the sender's official status or support route; never ask them to reveal an OTP.
Record whether incoming SMS, outgoing SMS or both fail.
Ask messaging support to verify the service-center profile; do not invent a number for the customer to enter.
Ask whether the affected sender appears in the device's blocked or filtered messages.
Record whether other messages arrive and use only the device's supported filtering controls with consent.
Record the port-completion date and whether voice calls now work.
Collect failed SMS times and sender networks for a routing trace; do not treat working calls as proof SMS routing is complete.
Record the purchased speed, upgrade date and a wired speed measurement if available.
Ask support to compare the purchased tier with the provisioned speed profile; Wi-Fi speed alone cannot verify the line tier.
Record the affected wired device and its negotiated link speed, if displayed.
If not already tried, compare a compatible known-good Ethernet cable; retain the before-and-after link readings.
Record wired speeds at a quiet time and during the recurring busy period.
Record whether the physical line remains connected and whether other customers report the same timing.
Ask whether backups, uploads or cameras are active when calls or browsing slow down.
With consent, briefly pause the identified upload and compare the connection; do not disable security services indiscriminately.
Record whether all IPTV channels buffer and whether the set-top box uses Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Compare other streaming services during the same failure and record whether they remain usable.
Record the missing channel or package and whether the provider bill shows the purchase.
Ask whether free channels or the local box menu work; a missing entitlement is different from a blank display.
Ask whether the TV shows the set-top box's local menu and confirm the selected TV input.
If safe and not already tried, compare a compatible known-good HDMI cable; record whether the local menu returns.
Record the affected channel, time and whether other channels work.
Check the provider's confirmed content-incident status rather than repeatedly resetting the box.
Record the outgoing-call error and whether incoming calls or data still work.
Ask support to check account restrictions through authentication; do not change barring codes from an unverified guide.
Record failed-call times, locations and whether the calls fail while moving.
Ask network support to compare the failures with handover traces; signal bars alone do not identify the fault.
Record the handset model and whether data works while voice calls fail.
Ask support to verify device compatibility and the line's voice-registration profile.
Record which calls are diverted and whether the customer recognises the forwarding destination.
Review forwarding settings through authenticated support with consent; do not publish destination numbers in chat.
Record the rooms where Wi-Fi fails and whether it improves near the router.
Ask whether Ethernet stays connected during the same problem; do not label a Wi-Fi coverage issue as a line outage.
WF01.title: Wi-Fi weak in some rooms while the line works
WF01.agent_checks: Ask wireless support to compare signal readings in affected rooms with a location near the router and verify that the wired connection stays stable.
WF01.completion: wireless signal and browsing improve in the previously affected rooms
WF01.diagnostic_gate: a wireless survey confirms weak signal in the affected rooms while the wired connection remains stable
WF01.action: agree an approved router position or compatible coverage extender with wireless support

customer_checks: Record whether all wireless devices fail and whether Ethernet stays connected at the same time.
Compare a wireless device near the router with the affected room and record where drops occur; keep the wired result for comparison.
WF02.title: Wi-Fi drops on multiple devices while Ethernet works
WF02.agent_checks: Ask wireless support to measure channel interference and confirm that simultaneous wired tests and the router internet connection remain normal.
WF02.completion: wireless retries decrease and the affected devices remain connected during the original problem period
WF02.diagnostic_gate: a wireless survey confirms channel interference while simultaneous wired tests and the router internet connection remain normal
WF02.action: have wireless support select an approved channel and recheck device compatibility

customer_checks: Record the appliance model and which Wi-Fi bands it supports.
Check whether the router advertises a compatible band and security mode; do not weaken security merely to force a connection.
Record the affected laptop and the exact connection error; confirm other devices still connect.
Ask whether the Wi-Fi name or password recently changed; credentials should be entered locally, not shared in chat.
